BEFORE THE PUBLIC SERVICE COMMISSION
                  OF THE STATE OF MISSOURI
 In the Matter of Evergy Metro, Inc. d/b/a Evergy    )
 Missouri Metro’s Request for Authority to           )      Case No. ER-2026-0143
 Implement a General Rate Increase for Electric      )
 Service

   ORDER GRANTING MOTION TO STRIKE AND MOTION FOR EXPEDITED
                         TREATMENT

Issue Date: September 28, 2026                            Effective Date: September 28, 2026

        On September 14, 2026, Evergy Metro, Inc. d/b/a Evergy Missouri Metro (Evergy

Metro) filed a motion asking the Commission to strike a portion of the prefiled direct

testimony of Staff’s witness, Sarah Lange. The portion of Lange’s testimony to which Evergy

Metro objects relates to information gathered by Lange during a tour of a non-utility party’s

facility.

        Evergy Metro objects to the inclusion of information acquired during the facility tour

because the testimony was developed by circumventing the entry-upon-land procedures in

the Commission’s rules, the opinions are based upon data not reasonably relied upon by

experts in the field, and the statements that the testimony relies on are hearsay from

declarants that no party can cross-examine. The Commission directed its Staff (Staff) to

respond to Evergy Metro’s motion to strike.

        In its response to Evergy Metro’s motion to strike, Staff states that the facility tour

was conducted in connection with the regulatory inspection activities of the Commission’s

Manufactured Housing Department and that Lange chose to attend to gather information for

this rate case. Staff argues that any concerns about the testimony’s foundation, reliability,
 hearsay, or the weight can be addressed through discovery, cross-examination, rebuttal

evidence, and, where appropriate, specific objections to particular evidence. However,

surrebuttal has already been filed, and the evidentiary hearing starts next week on October

5, 2026.

       Staff asserts that the question is whether Missouri Court Rule 58.01, concerning

document production and entry onto land prohibits the Commission from acting pursuant

to statutory authority or from conducting an authorized regulatory inspection because the

property owner is also a party to a contested case. Staff relies on Lange having undertaken

the tour pursuant to the Commission’s regulatory responsibilities.

       However, the facility owner is a party in this case, but it is not a Commission regulated

utility and the Commission’s jurisdiction is limited. Staff’s assertion that this tour was an

inspection pursuant to its regulatory obligations is somewhat disingenuous given that Lange

was there to gather information for this case. Staff’s response states: “Ms. Lange chose to

attend to see what, if any, information from the tour would be helpful for the Commission in

deciding this case.”

       The fact that Lange took the tour and asked questions is not in itself inappropriate,

but when the information from the tour becomes the rationale for a Staff proposed

disallowance then the appropriate method to make that information useful is to follow up

on it with appropriate discovery requests.

       Lange’s direct testimony, to the extent that it is opining on information gathered

during a tour organized for the Commission’s Manufactured Housing Department is

improper. Staff has not indicated that the tour provider would be a witness in this case.


                                               2
 Because it was used in testimony, and not just to satisfy her curiosity or address a

Commission inspection issue, Lange essentially conducted an informal deposition on a

witness unavailable to cross-examine at hearing.

       The Commission will grant Evergy Metro’s request to strike Lange’s tour related

testimony. However, the Commission will grant Staff the opportunity to provide conforming

testimony.

       THE COMMISSION ORDERS THAT:

       1.     Evergy Metro’s Motion to strike portions of the prepared direct testimony of

Lange is granted.

       2.     The specific portions of Lange’s direct testimony stricken are contained in

Appendix A to Evergy Missouri Metro’s Motion to Strike Portions of The Direct Testimony of

Staff Witness Sarah Lange.

       3.     Staff may file conforming testimony no later than October 1, 2026. Any

objections or responses to conforming Lange direct testimony will be addressed at the

evidentiary hearing.

       4.     This order is effective when issued.
